intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and rappels, this eco-adventure offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, three-toed sloths, and over 300 bird species in their natural habitat. Seasonal sea turtle nesting (July–October) makes this an unmissable eco-experience.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide. Trek jungle trails leading to pristine white-sand beaches while spotting white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs. The hike ends at Playa Manuel Antonio for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Night Jungle Walk & Hot Springs
experiences.description: Embark on a guided nocturnal jungle walk around the base of Arenal Volcano to discover Costa Rica's nighttime wildlife including tree frogs, tarantulas, and kinkajous. Cap the evening soaking in natural volcanic hot springs surrounded by lush rainforest — a perfect blend of adventure and relaxation.
experiences.location: La Fortuna de San Carlos, Alajuela Province

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Rainforest Expedition
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on a full-day guided trek through Corcovado National Park. Encounter Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four Costa Rican monkey species. This remote Osa Peninsula gem is a bucket-list eco-adventure for serious wildlife enthusiasts.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked shared shuttle or public bus to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront accommodation.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In transit
meals.lunch: N/A - In transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick and affordable bite at the airport food court (sodas or local fast food options around $5-8 USD) before or after landing, or pick up snacks at a convenience store near the resort.

day_by_day.notes: Keep your travel documents, colones (local currency), and a small amount of USD handy. Download the Uber app as it works in Costa Rica and is often cheaper than taxis. Pre-arrange your shuttle to avoid overpriced airport taxis. Rest well — big adventures start tomorrow!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a late wake-up, take a leisurely walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the immediate shoreline, watch for coastal wildlife such as pelicans, frigate birds, and hermit crabs. Collect your bearings and orientate yourself to the local area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest local market or 'soda' (traditional Costa Rican diner) in the nearby town. Pick up fresh tropical fruits — mangoes, papayas, and pineapples — at budget prices. Spend the afternoon relaxing on the beach, swimming, and watching for wildlife in the tidal pools. Look for iguanas sunbathing on rocks near the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beach at sunset — Costa Rican sunsets are spectacular and completely free. Head to a local soda for a traditional dinner. Ask locals for recommendations on the nearest budget-friendly spots.

meals.breakfast: Casado breakfast at the resort or a nearby soda — rice, beans, eggs, and fresh fruit for around $4-6 USD.
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit from the local market ($2-3 USD) and a light snack from a street vendor.
meals.dinner: Traditional 'Casado' plate (rice, black beans, salad, plantains, and protein) at a local soda for $6-9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect sunny skies and warm temperatures (28-33°C / 82-91°F). Apply sunscreen generously. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican colones for better rates at local markets and sodas.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the beach and surrounding jungle edges near the resort. February is excellent for spotting howler monkeys, scarlet macaws, and coatis. Bring binoculars if available. Walk quietly and slowly for best wildlife sightings. Start by 6:00-7:00 AM when animals are most active.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange a budget zip-lining excursion through a local operator near the resort area. Many coastal areas of Costa Rica offer zip-lining through jungle canopy for $30-50 USD per person when booked locally rather than through hotel desks. Ask at the resort front desk for the most affordable local operator. Zip-lining typically lasts 2-3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort and cool off with a swim. Watch for bioluminescence in the ocean after dark if conditions allow — a magical free natural experience. Head to a beachside 'rancho' bar for a cold Imperial beer ($1.50-2 USD) and light snacks.

meals.breakfast: Gallo pinto (rice and beans) with eggs and coffee at a local soda — $4-5 USD. Costa Rica's national breakfast dish.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch of bread, local cheese, and fruit from the market before the zip-lining excursion — $3-4 USD total.
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish at a beachside restaurant — look for 'catch of the day' specials for $8-12 USD including rice and salad.

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining directly with local operators rather than through the hotel to save 20-40%. Wear closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing. Bring a small backpack with water and sunscreen. Tip your zip-line guides $2-3 USD — it goes a long way locally.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget-friendly day trip to a nearby national park or wildlife reserve. Depending on the resort's exact location, options may include Manuel Antonio, Carara, or a local biological reserve. Arrive early (7:00-8:00 AM) for the best wildlife viewing. Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, and toucans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park. Hike one of the marked trails through the rainforest. Many coastal parks have trails leading to secluded beaches accessible only on foot. Swim at a pristine park beach and snorkel if you have gear (rental available for $5-8 USD at park entrances).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Rinse off and relax. Explore the local town on foot in the evening — browse local artisan shops for budget souvenirs (handmade bracelets, painted gourds, coffee). Enjoy a casual dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or pack snacks from the market — bananas, granola bars, and water for the park visit.
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch to avoid expensive park concessions — sandwiches, fruit, and plenty of water. Save $8-12 USD compared to park restaurants.
meals.dinner: Chicken or beef empanadas from a street vendor ($1-2 each) followed by a bowl of sopa negra (black bean soup) at a local soda — total $7-9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: National park entrance fees typically range from $18-20 USD per person. Arrive at opening time (7:00 AM) to beat crowds and see the most wildlife. Bring insect repellent, a rain jacket, and at least 2 liters of water per person. Wildlife is most active in the early morning and late afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga or meditation on the beach (free or $5-10 USD for a group class if available locally). Alternatively, take an early morning kayaking session along the coastline — rentals available for $10-15 USD per hour. Paddle through calm morning waters and look for sea turtles, rays, and coastal birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget snorkeling tour or rent equipment independently and snorkel from the beach. Costa Rican Pacific waters are rich with marine life — parrotfish, angelfish, sea turtles, and occasionally dolphins. Look for local guides offering informal snorkel tours for $15-25 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local 'pulpería' (corner store) and stock up on snacks and drinks for a budget beach picnic dinner. Watch the stars from the beach — with minimal light pollution in coastal Costa Rica, stargazing is spectacular. Look for the Southern Cross constellation.

meals.breakfast: Smoothie bowl or fresh fruit plate from a beachside café — $4-6 USD. Costa Rica's tropical fruits are exceptional.
meals.lunch: Ceviche from a local beach shack — fresh fish marinated in lime juice with cilantro and onions for $5-8 USD. A Costa Rican coastal staple.
meals.dinner: Budget beach picnic: local bread, cheese, deli meats, chips, and cold drinks from the pulpería — $6-8 USD total for a relaxing evening meal.

day_by_day.notes: Always snorkel with a buddy and never touch coral reefs. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only. The best snorkeling is typically in the morning when waters are calmer and clearer. Stay hydrated throughout the day — tropical heat can be deceptive.

day_by_day.morning: Arrange a guided bird-watching walk with a local naturalist guide. Costa Rica is one of the world's top bird-watching destinations with over 900 species. Local guides typically charge $20-35 USD for a 2-3 hour morning walk. Look for scarlet macaws, resplendent quetzals (if in highland areas), toucans, and motmots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or coffee plantation for a self-guided or budget tour ($10-15 USD). Learn about sustainable agriculture, taste fresh coffee at the source, and understand Costa Rica's famous 'Pura Vida' philosophy. Many farms offer free samples of tropical fruits grown on-site.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free cultural event or local football (soccer) match if available in the nearest town. Costa Ricans are passionate about football and matches are a great way to experience local culture. Grab street food from vendors around the stadium or town square.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Costa Rican breakfast at a family-run soda: gallo pinto, natilla (sour cream), and fresh orange juice — $5-7 USD.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the farm or plantation if included in the tour, or a simple rice and beans plate at a local soda — $4-6 USD.
meals.dinner: Street food evening: grilled corn (elote), plantain chips, and a meat skewer from town vendors — $5-7 USD total.

day_by_day.notes: Hiring a local naturalist guide for bird-watching not only enhances your experience but directly supports the local economy. Ask your resort to recommend trusted local guides. Bring a field guide app like Merlin Bird ID (free) on your phone for bird identification.

day_by_day.morning: Full day eco-adventure: arrange a whitewater rafting trip on a nearby river. Costa Rica offers rafting on rivers ranging from beginner (Class II) to expert (Class V). Budget operators offer half-day trips starting from $35-55 USD including equipment and a basic lunch. Book through local operators for best prices.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the rafting adventure or, if a half-day trip, return and spend the afternoon at a natural waterfall. Many areas near Costa Rica's coast have accessible waterfalls reachable by short hikes. Swimming in a natural waterfall pool is one of the most refreshing and memorable experiences in Costa Rica.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover from the active day. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer dinner as a mid-trip reward — try a restaurant with live marimba music, a traditional Costa Rican instrument. Enjoy a glass of Guaro (local sugarcane spirit) or a fresh agua dulce (hot sugarcane water).

meals.breakfast: Energy-rich breakfast before rafting: eggs, toast, peanut butter, and a banana — $5-6 USD at a soda.
meals.lunch: Typically included with rafting tour: rice, beans, salad, and fresh fruit at the riverside camp.
meals.dinner: Slightly splurge dinner at a local restaurant with character: grilled chicken or fish with plantains, rice, and salad — $12-15 USD. A well-deserved mid-trip treat.

day_by_day.notes: Rafting companies provide helmets, life jackets, and paddles. Wear quick-dry clothing and secure sandals or water shoes. Leave valuables at the resort. Waterproof your phone or leave it behind. Tip your rafting guides $3-5 USD — they work hard for your safety and fun.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and spend time journaling or reading on the beach. This is an intentional recovery day after intense activities. Take a gentle swim and practice floating in the ocean — a meditative and restorative experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local town on foot or by bicycle (rental $8-12 USD/day). Visit the local church, central park (every Costa Rican town has one), and browse the mercado municipal (municipal market) for local handicrafts, spices, and fresh produce. Chat with vendors and practice basic Spanish phrases.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from the market if your accommodation has kitchen access, or enjoy a relaxed dinner at a soda. Watch the sunset from the beach with a cold drink. Write postcards to send home — a budget and thoughtful souvenir tradition.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort or a café: fresh fruit platter, yogurt, and Costa Rican coffee — $5-7 USD.
meals.lunch: Market lunch: fresh vegetables, local cheese, artisan bread, and tropical fruit from market stalls — $4-5 USD.
meals.dinner: Simple soda dinner: arroz con pollo (rice with chicken) — a budget staple that's filling and delicious — $6-8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are essential on active eco-adventure trips. Use this time to do laundry (many hostels and budget hotels have laundry facilities for $3-5 USD), recharge electronics, review upcoming days' plans, and connect with fellow travelers for tips on hidden gems.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife spotting at a nearby mangrove estuary. Mangroves are incredible ecosystems teeming with wildlife — crocodiles, caimans, herons, kingfishers, and roosting bats. Arrange a budget boat tour ($15-25 USD per person) or kayak through the mangroves independently if rentals are available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a sea turtle conservation project if one operates near the resort area. Many coastal areas of Costa Rica have volunteer-run turtle monitoring programs that welcome eco-tourists. Learn about nesting sea turtles (Olive Ridley, Leatherback, or Green turtles depending on location) and conservation efforts.
day_by_day.evening: If timing is right, join a guided nighttime turtle nesting walk on the beach ($20-30 USD with a certified guide). Witnessing a sea turtle nest is a profoundly moving wildlife experience. If not available, enjoy a quiet beach walk and listen to the sounds of the rainforest at night.

meals.breakfast: Early, light breakfast before the mangrove tour: toast, banana, and coffee — $3-4 USD.
meals.lunch: Fresh coconut water straight from the coconut ($1-2 USD) and a plate of patacones (fried plantains) with black bean dip at a beachside stand — $4-5 USD.
meals.dinner: Seafood rice ('arroz con mariscos') at a local restaurant — $9-12 USD. A Costa Rican coastal specialty worth trying.

day_by_day.notes: Always use certified, responsible guides for turtle watching. Never use flash photography around turtles. Follow all guide instructions strictly. February is a good month for Olive Ridley turtle activity on the Pacific coast. Conservation fees often go directly to protecting nesting beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day trip to a nearby cloud forest or higher elevation area if accessible from the resort location. The change in ecosystem from beach to cloud forest is dramatic and offers completely different wildlife — resplendent quetzals, cloud forest orchids, and misty hanging bridges. Shared shuttles make this affordable ($20-35 USD round trip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk a hanging bridges trail through the cloud forest canopy. Hanging bridges offer a bird's-eye view of the forest at treetop level — a different perspective from zip-lining and perfect for wildlife photography. Look for howler monkeys, sloths, and colorful poison dart frogs on the forest floor below.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy a warm shower after the cooler cloud forest temperatures. Relax with fellow travelers and share stories over dinner. Costa Rica's traveler community is friendly and tips flow freely between adventurers.

meals.breakfast: Pack a breakfast to eat on the shuttle: bananas, granola bars, and a thermos of Costa Rican coffee — $2-3 USD.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a cloud forest soda or visitor center: typical casado plate — $7-9 USD. Portions are generous.
meals.dinner: Back at the coast: grilled whole fish ('pescado entero') with rice, salad, and patacones — $10-13 USD at a beachside restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a light rain jacket and an extra layer for the cloud forest — temperatures can be 10-15°C cooler than the coast. Wear sturdy walking shoes. The contrast between ecosystems in a single day is one of Costa Rica's most remarkable travel experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Surfing lesson on the beach. Costa Rica's Pacific coast is world-famous for surfing, and February offers excellent conditions. Budget surf schools offer 2-hour lessons including board and instruction for $25-40 USD per person. Even complete beginners can stand up on a board in calm beach break conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue surfing independently (board rental $10-15 USD/hour after the lesson) or explore a different section of coastline. Look for tide pools at low tide — they're fascinating micro-ecosystems filled with sea urchins, starfish, small fish, and anemones. Check tide tables at the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your surfing achievement with a bonfire on the beach if permitted, or join other travelers for a beach gathering. Many budget beach destinations in Costa Rica have informal evening gatherings. Enjoy local craft beers or fresh coconut cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Protein-rich breakfast before surfing: scrambled eggs with gallo pinto and fresh juice — $5-6 USD.
meals.lunch: Beachside burrito or wrap from a food truck or beach shack — $5-7 USD. Quick and convenient between surf sessions.
meals.dinner: Celebrate with a pizza at a local Italian-Costa Rican fusion spot (common in beach towns) — $8-11 USD. A nice change of pace from traditional food.

day_by_day.notes: Always surf with awareness of rip currents. Ask your surf instructor about local water conditions and hazards. Never surf alone, especially as a beginner. Apply waterproof sunscreen before entering the water. Surfing is one of Costa Rica's most joyful and accessible budget activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final full adventure day: book a combo eco-adventure package combining multiple activities. Many local operators offer combination deals — for example, zip-lining + horseback riding + waterfall visit for $50-70 USD — significantly cheaper than booking each separately. Horseback riding through jungle trails to a waterfall is a quintessential Costa Rican experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local wildlife rescue center or sanctuary. These facilities rehabilitate injured and orphaned wildlife and offer educational tours ($10-20 USD). See sloths, spider monkeys, toucans, and coatis up close in a responsible, conservation-focused environment. A deeply rewarding experience that directly funds animal care.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening souvenir shopping. Look for authentic Costa Rican crafts: Boruca tribal masks, painted ox-cart miniatures, shade-grown coffee, and local chocolate. Bargain respectfully at markets. Pack purchases carefully to avoid damage. Enjoy a final celebratory dinner with your best meal of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Energy breakfast for the adventure day: pancakes with local honey and fresh fruit at a café — $6-8 USD.
meals.lunch: Typically included in the combo adventure package, or a quick stop at a local soda during the tour.
meals.dinner: Splurge final dinner: whole lobster or jumbo shrimp if on the Pacific coast, or a traditional 'olla de carne' (beef and vegetable stew) — $15-20 USD. Your most memorable meal of the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Use this last full day to complete any experiences you missed earlier in the trip. Purchase coffee directly from a local farm or cooperative — it's far cheaper and better quality than airport shops. Pack souvenirs in your checked luggage to avoid issues at security. Set an early alarm for tomorrow's departure preparations.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk on the beach — take it all in one last time. Breathe the ocean air, watch the pelicans dive, and listen to the howler monkeys in the distance. Pack your bags carefully and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage with the front desk if your flight departs later in the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, enjoy a final swim in the ocean, a last cup of Costa Rican coffee at a beachside café, or a slow walk through town. Visit the local market one final time for any last-minute food souvenirs — vacuum-packed coffee, local hot sauce (Salsa Lizano), and dried tropical fruits travel well.
day_by_day.evening: Arrange transport to Juan Santamaría International Airport (allow 3-4 hours for travel plus check-in for international flights). Arrive at the airport with ample time. Spend any remaining colones on snacks and drinks before the security checkpoint — colones are difficult to exchange outside Costa Rica.

meals.breakfast: Final gallo pinto breakfast at a local soda — a proper Costa Rican farewell meal for $4-6 USD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch before departure: fresh fruit, a sandwich, or empanadas from a local bakery — $4-5 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight dining. If time allows before security, the airport has a few sodas serving traditional food at reasonable prices ($8-12 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Reconfirm your return flight 24 hours before departure. Keep all receipts for customs declarations if required. Costa Rica has a departure tax that may or may not be included in your ticket — check in advance. Carry your passport and boarding pass in an easily accessible pocket. Pura Vida — may the spirit of Costa Rica travel home with you!

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and meet your pre-arranged private transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome drink at the resort bar if still open, and settle into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: N/A – In-flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: N/A – In-flight meal
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport convenience store or resort welcome amenity upon check-in

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your airport transfer in advance to avoid taxi hassles at night. Keep essentials in your carry-on for easy access. Exchange a small amount of currency (colones) at the airport for tips and incidentals.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort restaurant overlooking the beachfront. Take a slow walk along the beach to get your bearings and soak in the Pacific coastal scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation afternoon: explore the resort grounds, book upcoming excursions at the concierge desk, and take a refreshing swim in the ocean or resort pool. Visit the nearby local village on foot or by tuk-tuk to browse souvenir shops and get a feel for the local culture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's beachfront terrace. Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the resort restaurant, sampling Costa Rican staples like gallo pinto and fresh ceviche.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – enjoy fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee (included or ~$12–15 USD)
meals.lunch: Casual soda (local diner) near the resort – casado (rice, beans, plantains, protein) for ~$8–10 USD
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant – fresh grilled fish or shrimp with local sides, ~$20–28 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest and acclimatization day. Costa Rica's time zone is CST (UTC-6). Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen – the equatorial sun is intense even in February.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by shuttle or private transfer toward Manuel Antonio National Park (approximately 1–2.5 hours depending on resort location). Arrive for the Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike starting at 8:00 AM with a certified naturalist guide. Trek jungle trails spotting white-faced capuchin monkeys, sloths, scarlet macaws, coatis, and Jesus Christ lizards.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the guided hike, spend the afternoon relaxing on the stunning white-sand beaches within the national park boundary (Playa Manuel Antonio or Playa Espadilla Sur). Snorkel in the calm cove, swim, or simply birdwatch from the shoreline.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the town of Quepos (10 minutes from Manuel Antonio) for dinner at a local restaurant with ocean views. Return to the resort by private transfer or stay overnight near Manuel Antonio if distance requires.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at resort or packed fruit and granola bar before departure
meals.lunch: Beachside soda or food kiosk inside/near Manuel Antonio park – fresh coconut, empanadas, and fruit plates, ~$8–12 USD
meals.dinner: El Patio de Café Milagro in Quepos – fusion Costa Rican cuisine with tropical cocktails, ~$18–25 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio park has a daily visitor cap – book your guided hike and park entrance tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance. Bring biodegradable sunscreen (required in the park), insect repellent, and a dry bag for beach time. Monkeys are bold – secure your belongings.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the scenic transfer toward the Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours by shuttle with scenic stops). Depart by 7:00 AM. Stop en route at a roadside mirador (viewpoint) for photos of the Central Valley and volcanic landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in La Fortuna, the gateway town to Arenal Volcano. Check into your mid-range lodge or use as a base. Explore La Fortuna town center, visit the La Fortuna Waterfall (a 70-meter cascade reached via a 500-step descent through the rainforest – ~$18 USD entrance). Swim in the natural pool at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Arenal Volcano Night Jungle Walk & Hot Springs: Embark on a guided nocturnal jungle walk around the base of Arenal Volcano. Discover nocturnal wildlife including tree frogs, kinkajous, tarantulas, and exotic insects. Afterward, soak in natural volcanic hot spring pools under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Roadside Tico restaurant en route – hearty casado with fresh juice, ~$9–12 USD
meals.dinner: Don Rufino Restaurant in La Fortuna – upscale Tico cuisine, grilled meats and local fish, ~$20–30 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: The night jungle walk typically starts at 5:30–6:00 PM and lasts 2 hours, followed by hot springs access. Book the Arenal Night Walk + Hot Springs combo package (~$55–75 USD per person) through a reputable operator like Desafío Adventure Co. Wear long pants and closed-toe shoes for the night walk.

day_by_day.morning: Full morning at leisure in the Arenal area. Optional: Kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding on Lake Arenal with stunning volcano backdrop (~$35–45 USD). Alternatively, visit the Arenal Hanging Bridges for a self-guided walk through the rainforest canopy on suspension bridges with excellent birdwatching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local chocolate or coffee farm near La Fortuna for a guided tasting tour (~$25–35 USD) – learn about the farm-to-cup process of Costa Rican cacao and coffee. Browse artisan crafts and local markets in La Fortuna town.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at Baldi Hot Springs or Tabacón Hot Springs (mid-range option ~$40–60 USD) for a second evening soak. Enjoy the resort-style thermal pools with swim-up bars and lush tropical gardens.

meals.breakfast: Soda La Parada in La Fortuna – traditional gallo pinto, eggs, fresh fruit, and coffee, ~$8–10 USD
meals.lunch: Rancho La Cascada restaurant – open-air Tico buffet near the waterfall area, ~$10–14 USD
meals.dinner: Lava Lounge La Fortuna – casual international and Tico fusion, burgers, wraps, and local dishes, ~$15–20 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: La Fortuna Waterfall is best visited in the morning before crowds arrive. Baldi Hot Springs offers a good mid-range value with 25 pools at varying temperatures. Keep your camera dry – afternoon rain showers are common in February.

day_by_day.morning: Depart La Fortuna by 7:00 AM via the scenic Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer across Lake Arenal (a classic Costa Rican adventure route, ~$30 USD per person) heading toward Monteverde Cloud Forest. Enjoy stunning views of the lake and surrounding mountains during the 3-hour journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde/Santa Elena by midday. Check into your mid-range cloud forest lodge. Explore the Santa Elena town center, browse local artisan shops, and visit the Bat Jungle or Serpentarium for an educational wildlife encounter (~$15 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a farm-to-table dinner at a local Monteverde restaurant. Take an optional guided night walk at the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve (~$25 USD) to spot nocturnal cloud forest species including glass frogs, owls, and porcupines.

meals.breakfast: Quick grab-and-go breakfast before Jeep-Boat-Jeep departure – packed fruit, bread, and coffee from a La Fortuna bakery
meals.lunch: Café Colibri in Santa Elena – fresh sandwiches, salads, and smoothies, ~$10–14 USD
meals.dinner: Trio Restaurant Monteverde – creative Costa Rican cuisine with cloud forest ambiance, ~$18–25 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: The Jeep-Boat-Jeep transfer is a fun and scenic alternative to a long road journey – book it the day before through your hotel. Monteverde sits at 1,440 meters elevation – temperatures are cooler (15–22°C), so pack a light jacket and rain layer.

day_by_day.morning: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour: The highlight of the trip! Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience multiple cables, Tarzan swings, rappelling, and a Superman cable with panoramic views over the forest. Tours typically depart at 8:00 AM (~$50–80 USD per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve for a 2-hour self-guided or guided afternoon walk (~$25 USD entrance). Spot resplendent quetzals (February is peak quetzal season!), emerald toucanets, and howler monkeys in the cloud forest.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cheese tasting at one of Monteverde's famous local dairy farms (the region is renowned for its artisan cheese). Enjoy a relaxed dinner back in Santa Elena with live marimba music at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort or lodge breakfast – fuel up before the zip-line adventure
meals.lunch: Soda Sara in Santa Elena – authentic home-cooked Tico food, ~$8–11 USD
meals.dinner: Morpho's Restaurant Santa Elena – locally loved, generous portions of traditional Costa Rican dishes, ~$14–20 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: February is one of the best months to spot the resplendent quetzal in Monteverde – hire a specialized quetzal guide for the afternoon walk for the best chance of a sighting (~$20–30 USD for a 2-hour guided walk). The zip-line tour requires closed-toe shoes and no loose jewelry.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided birdwatching walk in the Children's Eternal Rainforest (Bosque Eterno de los Niños) – the largest private reserve in Costa Rica. Spot hummingbirds, motmots, and trogons with a local birding expert (~$30–40 USD including guide).
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Monteverde toward the Caribbean coast to position for the Tortuguero adventure (approximately 4–5 hours via shuttle to San José, then onward connection). Alternatively, spend the afternoon at the Monteverde Butterfly Garden or Orchid Garden (~$12–15 USD each) if the transfer is the following morning.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in San José or Guápiles area for an overnight stay at a mid-range hotel en route to Tortuguero. Explore the local area and enjoy a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Cloud forest lodge breakfast – enjoy the cool mountain morning air with hot coffee and local pastries
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant en route – casado or arroz con pollo, ~$9–12 USD
meals.dinner: Local Tico restaurant near overnight stop – simple, hearty Caribbean-influenced cuisine, ~$12–18 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is only accessible by boat or small plane – most travelers transit through Cariari or La Pavona to take the canal boat into the park. Pre-book your Tortuguero lodge and boat transfer at least 2 weeks in advance. This is a transit day, so keep luggage streamlined.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by bus/shuttle to La Pavona dock (approximately 1.5–2 hours from Guápiles). Board a covered motorized canoe through the jungle canals for the scenic 1.5-hour boat ride to Tortuguero village. Check into your mid-range jungle lodge on the canal.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari. Spot caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, great green macaws, poison dart frogs, river otters, and manatees. Your naturalist guide will interpret the incredible biodiversity of this UNESCO-listed wetland ecosystem.
day_by_day.evening: Walk through Tortuguero village – a charming, car-free community accessible only by boat. Visit the Sea Turtle Conservancy visitor center to learn about the legendary green sea turtle nesting program. Enjoy dinner at a local Caribbean-style restaurant overlooking the canal.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at overnight hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tortuguero jungle lodge upon arrival – fresh Caribbean rice and beans with coconut milk (arroz con leche caribeño), ~$10–14 USD
meals.dinner: Miss Junie's Restaurant Tortuguero – legendary Caribbean home cooking, fresh fish, rice and beans, plantains, ~$14–18 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is hot and humid (28–32°C) with frequent rain – pack a lightweight rain poncho, insect repellent with DEET, and waterproof bags for electronics. The boat safari is best in early morning or late afternoon when wildlife is most active. February is the dry season on the Caribbean coast – excellent wildlife viewing conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise kayak or canoe paddle through the narrow secondary canals of Tortuguero (self-guided or with guide, ~$20–30 USD kayak rental). These smaller waterways offer intimate wildlife encounters impossible from motorized boats – spot poison dart frogs, basilisk lizards, and exotic birds at eye level.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Cerro de Tortuguero trail – a short but steep jungle hike to the highest point in the area offering panoramic views over the canal network and Caribbean Sea. Afterward, relax at the lodge pool or take a swim at the beach (check conditions with locals first).
day_by_day.evening: Optional night boat tour through the canals (~$25 USD) to spotlight nocturnal wildlife including caimans, sleeping birds, and tree frogs. Return for a farewell Caribbean dinner at the lodge.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruits, eggs, and Caribbean-style coffee
meals.lunch: Buddha Café Tortuguero – light wraps, fresh juices, and smoothies in a relaxed garden setting, ~$10–13 USD
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant – Caribbean lobster or snook with coconut rice, ~$18–24 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: The narrow secondary canals (caños) are the highlight of Tortuguero – don't skip the kayak experience. Bring binoculars for the Cerro hike. If visiting between July–October, green sea turtle nesting tours are available at night – February is outside nesting season but wildlife remains exceptional.

day_by_day.morning: One final early morning canal walk or birding session before checkout. Depart Tortuguero by boat back to La Pavona dock (7:30 AM boat recommended). Transfer by shuttle toward the Osa Peninsula / Corcovado region (approximately 5–6 hours total with connections via San José or domestic flight from San José to Puerto Jiménez).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Puerto Jiménez, the gateway to Corcovado National Park on the Osa Peninsula. Check into your mid-range eco-lodge. Explore the small town, visit the local market, and arrange final details for tomorrow's Corcovado expedition with your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the quiet Golfo Dulce shoreline at sunset. Enjoy a fresh seafood dinner at a local Puerto Jiménez restaurant, sampling the day's catch from local fishermen.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before boat departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or roadside stop en route – sandwich, fruit, and water
meals.dinner: Restaurante Carolina Puerto Jiménez – fresh grilled fish, ceviche, and cold Imperial beer, ~$14–20 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Consider a domestic flight from San José to Puerto Jiménez (Sansa Airlines, ~$80–120 USD one-way, 45 minutes) to save 4+ hours of road travel. Book well in advance as Osa Peninsula flights fill quickly. Corcovado requires advance park reservations and a certified guide – confirm your booking tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Corcovado National Park Rainforest Expedition: Depart at 5:30 AM by boat from Puerto Jiménez to La Leona or San Pedrillo ranger station. Begin a full-day guided trek deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests – home to all four Costa Rican monkey species (howler, spider, squirrel, and white-faced capuchin), Baird's tapirs, giant anteaters, pumas, and over 400 bird species including the scarlet macaw.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Corcovado expedition through primary rainforest trails. Swim in a pristine jungle river or waterfall during the midday break. Your certified naturalist guide will identify tracks, calls, and behaviors of Corcovado's extraordinary wildlife.
day_by_day.evening: Return by boat to Puerto Jiménez by 4:00–5:00 PM. Rest, shower, and celebrate the epic day with sundowners on the Golfo Dulce waterfront. Enjoy a special farewell dinner at the best local restaurant in town.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast at eco-lodge before 5:30 AM departure – eggs, toast, fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by tour operator or lodge – sandwiches, fruit, energy bars, and plenty of water (essential in Corcovado's heat)
meals.dinner: Jade Luna Restaurant Puerto Jiménez – upscale Osa Peninsula dining, fresh seafood and organic local ingredients, ~$22–30 USD per person

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado is the most demanding day of the trip – wear moisture-wicking clothing, sturdy waterproof hiking boots, and bring 3+ liters of water. The park entrance fee is ~$18 USD plus mandatory certified guide fee (~$60–80 USD). February offers excellent wildlife viewing with manageable trail conditions. This is considered one of the world's top wildlife experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica. Enjoy a slow, celebratory breakfast at your eco-lodge. Take a gentle walk along the Golfo Dulce beach for a last dose of Pacific coast tranquility. Pack souvenirs – locally made chocolate, coffee, artisan crafts, and hot sauce make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Puerto Jiménez to San José via domestic flight or shuttle (depart by noon depending on departure flight schedule). Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport with time to browse duty-free shops for Costa Rican coffee, Britt chocolates, and local rum.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of cloud forests, volcanic hot springs, jungle canals, zip-lines, and some of the world's most spectacular wildlife. ¡Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at eco-lodge – full Tico spread with fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto, and the best Costa Rican coffee of the trip
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or San José café en route – light meal before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in, security, and immigration at SJO airport. Confirm your domestic flight or shuttle transfer the evening before. Costa Rica charges a $29 USD departure tax (usually included in international airfare – verify with your airline). Keep $20–30 USD cash for final tips to guides, lodge staff, and drivers who made your journey exceptional.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. With over 13 cables, Tarzan swings, and rappels, this eco-adventure offers breathtaking views of the forest and occasional wildlife sightings including toucans and howler monkeys.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle canals of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari teeming with wildlife. Spot caimans, river turtles, Jesus Christ lizards, three-toed sloths, and over 300 bird species in their natural habitat. Seasonal sea turtle nesting (July–October) makes this an unmissable eco-experience.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore Costa Rica's most biodiverse national park with a certified naturalist guide. Trek jungle trails leading to pristine white-sand beaches while spotting white-faced capuchin monkeys, two-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs. The hike ends at Playa Manuel Antonio for a refreshing swim.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Night Jungle Walk & Hot Springs
experiences.description: Embark on a guided nocturnal jungle walk around the base of Arenal Volcano to discover Costa Rica's nighttime wildlife including tree frogs, tarantulas, and kinkajous. Cap the evening soaking in natural volcanic hot springs surrounded by lush rainforest — a perfect blend of adventure and relaxation.
experiences.location: La Fortuna de San Carlos, Alajuela Province

experiences.name: Corcovado National Park Rainforest Expedition
experiences.description: Venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on a full-day guided trek through Corcovado National Park. Encounter Baird's tapirs, white-lipped peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four Costa Rican monkey species. This remote Osa Peninsula gem is a bucket-list eco-adventure for serious wildlife enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – Late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. A private luxury transfer with a dedicated concierge will greet you at arrivals with refreshments. Enjoy a smooth, air-conditioned ride to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, receive a welcome cocktail and a brief orientation from the resort host. Settle into your beachfront suite.

meals.breakfast: N/A
meals.lunch: N/A
meals.dinner: Light welcome amenity in-suite: artisan cheese board, tropical fruit platter, and a bottle of sparkling wine arranged by the resort upon arrival.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 completely relaxed. Confirm all upcoming excursion bookings with the resort concierge before sleeping. Luggage unpacking service available upon request.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely start. Take a sunrise stroll along the private beachfront at Aegean Bliss Resort. Explore the resort grounds, swim in the infinity pool, or enjoy a 60-minute welcome massage at the resort spa to reset after travel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private resort orientation tour led by a naturalist guide. Explore the resort's on-site gardens, spot resident birds and reptiles, and learn about the local coastal ecosystem. Enjoy a private kayaking session in the calm coastal waters adjacent to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail hour on the resort's ocean-view terrace. Enjoy hand-crafted caipirinhas and Costa Rican rum cocktails while watching the Pacific sunset. Attend the resort's optional cultural presentation on Costa Rican biodiversity and conservation.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant featuring tropical fruits, freshly baked pastries, made-to-order eggs, and locally sourced coffee.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the resort's beach club: fresh ceviche, grilled mahi-mahi tacos, and chilled coconut water served directly to your lounger.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at the resort's signature restaurant. Begin with a hearts of palm salad, followed by pan-seared snapper with plantain purée and a passion fruit crème brûlée for dessert. Wine pairing available.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to fully recover from travel. Confirm transportation logistics for the Tortuguero excursion with the concierge. Request early morning packed breakfast for upcoming adventure days.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early by private charter flight or premium road transfer toward Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast. Upon arrival, board a private motorized canoe for the Tortuguero National Park Wildlife Boat Safari. Glide silently through jungle-lined canals spotting caimans, river turtles, howler monkeys, sloths, and a spectacular array of tropical birds including toucans and herons.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the wildlife boat safari deeper into Tortuguero's canal network. Disembark for a short guided walk along a jungle trail inside the park. Your certified naturalist guide will point out poison dart frogs, Jesus Christ lizards, and rare orchids. Return by boat to the lodge for a rest period.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sundowners aboard a private canal boat as the jungle transitions into its nocturnal chorus. Transfer back to base and either fly back or overnight at a premium eco-lodge in Tortuguero (Tortuga Lodge & Gardens recommended for its luxury positioning within the park area).

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by the resort: granola parfait, fresh fruit skewers, and a thermos of single-origin Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tortuga Lodge: Caribbean-style rice and beans with grilled chicken, fresh tropical salad, and fresh-squeezed lemonade.
meals.dinner: Candlelit dinner at Tortuga Lodge's open-air restaurant overlooking the canal: Caribbean lobster tail with coconut rice, sautéed vegetables, and a decadent chocolate lava cake.

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by air or boat — confirm charter arrangements at least 48 hours in advance. Bring binoculars, insect repellent, and light rain gear. February is generally dry on the Pacific side but the Caribbean coast may see brief showers.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bird-watching walk along Tortuguero's beach and canal banks with a private ornithologist guide. The dawn hours offer the best opportunity to spot the park's 400+ bird species. If visiting during nesting season, ask about guided sea turtle conservation observation (subject to seasonal availability).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return transfer to the Pacific coast by private charter. Upon arrival back at Aegean Bliss Resort, enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the resort spa with a choice of a jungle botanical body wrap or a deep-tissue massage. Decompress by the infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Private beachfire experience arranged by the resort: a personal butler sets up a fire pit on the beach with gourmet s'mores, tropical cocktails, and ambient music under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Tortuga Lodge before departure: scrambled eggs, gallo pinto (Costa Rican rice and beans), fresh tropical fruit, and café chorreado.
meals.lunch: Light in-flight or transfer snack box. Upon return to resort, order from the pool bar menu: shrimp ceviche tostadas and a fresh watermelon juice.
meals.dinner: Intimate beachside dinner at the resort: a private table on the sand with a four-course tasting menu featuring local ingredients — tuna tartare, hearts of palm bisque, grilled tenderloin with chimichurri, and a tres leches dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm the return charter timing with the concierge the night before. Allow buffer time for weather-related delays on the Caribbean coast. Spa bookings should be made 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer departs for Arenal Volcano region (approximately 3–4 hours depending on route). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Central Valley highlands. Upon arrival at the Arenal area, check in at a premium eco-lodge (The Springs Resort & Spa or Nayara Springs recommended) and enjoy panoramic volcano views from your private villa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arenal Volcano National Park on a guided afternoon hike through old lava fields and secondary rainforest. Your certified naturalist guide will explain the volcanic history and identify wildlife including coatis, agoutis, and colorful birds along the trail.
day_by_day.evening: Arenal Volcano Night Jungle Walk & Hot Springs: Embark on a guided nocturnal jungle walk around the base of Arenal Volcano. Discover Costa Rica's hidden nighttime world — red-eyed tree frogs, tarantulas, kinkajous, and bioluminescent fungi. Conclude the evening soaking in natural volcanic hot spring pools under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure: full à la carte service with eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: En route lunch stop at a premium restaurant in La Fortuna town: traditional Costa Rican casado with grilled fish, black beans, rice, and fried plantains.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the eco-lodge's signature restaurant after the hot springs: wood-fired pizza with local toppings, a shared charcuterie board, and locally brewed craft beer or fine wine.

day_by_day.notes: Pack a dry bag for the hot springs visit. Bring a headlamp for the night walk — the guide will provide one but having your own is recommended. Water shoes are useful for the hot spring pools.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding excursion on Lake Arenal with the volcano as your backdrop. The calm morning waters and misty atmosphere make for extraordinary photography. Spot kingfishers, ospreys, and basilisk lizards along the shoreline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Arenal Hanging Bridges — a premium guided walk through a series of suspension bridges spanning the rainforest canopy. Your naturalist guide will identify tree frogs, howler monkeys, and rare bromeliads at canopy level. This is a gentler, non-zip-line canopy experience ideal for wildlife observation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for a private couples' or solo sunset spa treatment at the volcanic hot spring spa. Enjoy a volcanic mud wrap followed by a soak in tiered thermal pools overlooking the volcano silhouette at dusk.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast delivered to your terrace: açaí bowl, avocado toast on sourdough, freshly pressed juices, and a French press of specialty Costa Rican coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch prepared by the lodge and enjoyed at a scenic viewpoint near the hanging bridges: gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, sparkling water, and artisan chocolate.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at The Springs Resort's Los Tucanes restaurant (or equivalent at chosen lodge): five-course tasting menu with wine pairing, featuring local ingredients such as heart of palm, guanacaste beef, and exotic tropical fruit desserts.

day_by_day.notes: Morning lake conditions are typically calm and ideal for paddling. Book the hanging bridges early entry slot (7:00 AM) for the best wildlife sightings before afternoon crowds arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal region by private luxury transfer heading toward Monteverde Cloud Forest (approximately 3 hours via the scenic lake route, including a short boat crossing on Lake Arenal — a highlight in itself). Arrive at Monteverde and check in at a premium cloud forest lodge (El Silencio Lodge & Spa or Belmar Hotel recommended).
day_by_day.afternoon: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience multiple zip lines ranging from gentle glides to high-speed runs through the cloud forest, including a Tarzan swing and hanging bridges. Your guides are certified professionals ensuring both safety and entertainment.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a premium artisan coffee and chocolate tour in Monteverde — learn the farm-to-cup journey of Costa Rican coffee and the bean-to-bar process of local dark chocolate. Conclude with a guided tasting of single-origin coffees and handcrafted chocolates paired with local cheese.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure: traditional gallo pinto, fresh tropical fruit, eggs to order, and café chorreado.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Santa Elena village (Monteverde's main town): gourmet farm-to-table restaurant featuring locally grown vegetables, artisan cheese from Monteverde's famous dairy cooperative, and fresh-baked bread.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the cloud forest lodge's restaurant: cream of chayote soup, pan-seared chicken with cloud forest mushroom sauce, roasted root vegetables, and a warm banana foster dessert.

day_by_day.notes: The Lake Arenal boat crossing adds approximately 30–45 minutes but is highly scenic and recommended. Dress in layers for Monteverde — the cloud forest is significantly cooler and mistier than the coast. Bring a light waterproof jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided walk through the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve at first light (6:30 AM entry). This is the optimal time to spot the legendary resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and other rare cloud forest species. Your expert ornithologist guide will use a spotting scope for close-up wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Orchid Garden — premium guided tours of these specialized ecosystems reveal the extraordinary biodiversity of the cloud forest at a micro level. Spot blue morpho butterflies, glass-wing species, and hundreds of rare orchid varieties in climate-controlled enclosures.
day_by_day.evening: Twilight guided walk in the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve — a smaller, less-visited reserve offering intimate wildlife encounters at dusk. Spot kinkajous, olingo, and various nocturnal insects before returning to the lodge for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the 6:30 AM forest walk: granola, yogurt, tropical fruit, and coffee prepared by the lodge at 6:00 AM.
meals.lunch: Late brunch back at the lodge after the morning walk: cloud forest mushroom omelette, avocado salad, freshly baked rolls, and a selection of herbal teas.
meals.dinner: Premium dining experience at Belmar Hotel's restaurant (or equivalent): a curated Costa Rican tasting menu with local wine and spirits pairing, featuring cloud forest-foraged ingredients and artisan Monteverde cheese.

day_by_day.notes: Quetzal sightings are most likely in February–April during nesting season — this trip timing is excellent. Request a specialized quetzal-focused guide through the lodge concierge. Wear dark or neutral-colored clothing for better wildlife viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Monteverde to Manuel Antonio on the central Pacific coast (approximately 4 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Central Pacific lowlands, passing through lush agricultural regions. Arrive at Manuel Antonio and check in at a premium hillside boutique hotel (La Mariposa Hotel or Arenas del Mar recommended for their eco-luxury positioning).
day_by_day.afternoon: Orientation walk along the Manuel Antonio beach area. Explore the resort's private access to the national park boundary. Spot white-faced capuchin monkeys, squirrel monkeys, and two-toed sloths in the trees immediately adjacent to the resort — Manuel Antonio is famous for wildlife visible even from the hotel grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktail cruise along the Manuel Antonio coastline aboard a private catamaran. Enjoy panoramic views of the Quepos coastline, spot dolphins and seabirds, and raise a glass of sparkling wine as the sun dips below the Pacific horizon.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before departure: full hot breakfast with eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: En route stop at a premium roadside restaurant near Quepos: fresh Pacific shrimp in garlic butter, rice, and a cold Imperial beer or fresh juice.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel's hilltop restaurant with panoramic ocean views: tuna tataki starter, creamy seafood bisque, grilled whole snapper with mango salsa, and a coconut panna cotta dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio has some of the highest biodiversity density in Costa Rica — wildlife is literally everywhere, including the resort grounds. Keep food secured as capuchin monkeys are clever thieves. Confirm catamaran sunset cruise booking 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike: Enter the park at opening (7:00 AM) with a certified naturalist guide for the best wildlife activity. Trek jungle trails and spot three species of monkeys (capuchin, squirrel, and howler), two and three-toed sloths, coatis, iguanas, and an extraordinary array of birds. Your guide uses a spotting scope to bring animals into close view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Manuel Antonio's stunning Playa Biesanz — a secluded, calm-water beach accessible via a short trail. Enjoy snorkeling in the crystal-clear waters (equipment provided by the hotel) or simply lounge under a palm tree with a good book. A beach butler from the hotel can arrange refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Private outdoor cinema experience at the resort: the hotel arranges a curated film screening on a private terrace under the stars, complete with gourmet popcorn, cocktails, and blankets.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before the 7:00 AM park entry: tropical smoothie bowl, avocado toast, scrambled eggs, and cold-brew coffee.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Playa Biesanz: the hotel prepares a premium beach picnic basket with fresh sandwiches, ceviche cups, tropical fruit, and sparkling water.
meals.dinner: Romantic dinner at Emilio's Café or Barba Roja restaurant in Manuel Antonio (or in-hotel fine dining): fresh lobster thermidor, grilled octopus starter, and a local guaro sour cocktail to begin.

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at the national park as early as possible — the park has a daily visitor cap and early entry guarantees the best wildlife activity. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only in the marine areas. The park closes at 4:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Manuel Antonio to Corcovado National Park region on the Osa Peninsula (approximately 3–4 hours or 30 minutes by private charter flight — charter is strongly recommended for comfort). Arrive at a luxury eco-lodge on the Osa Peninsula (Lapa Rios Lodge or El Remanso Lodge recommended — both are world-class eco-luxury properties).
day_by_day.afternoon: Corcovado National Park Rainforest Expedition: Venture deep into one of the world's most biologically intense rainforests on a guided trek. Accompanied by a certified park guide and your naturalist, explore primary rainforest trails teeming with scarlet macaws, tapirs, peccaries, four species of monkeys, and potentially jaguars (rare but possible). This is a full-immersion primary rainforest experience unlike anywhere else on Earth.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the eco-lodge for a restorative evening. Enjoy a private yoga session on the lodge's jungle-view platform as the forest sounds transition to nighttime. Decompress in a natural freshwater pool or outdoor shower surrounded by the rainforest.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Manuel Antonio hotel before transfer: continental spread with local cheeses, cured meats, tropical fruits, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch eaten inside Corcovado: the lodge prepares a premium trail lunch box — whole grain wraps, energy bars, fresh fruit, and electrolyte drinks.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the eco-lodge's open-air restaurant: farm-and-forest-to-table menu featuring Osa Peninsula ingredients — wild heart of palm soup, grilled local fish with yuca fries, and a dark chocolate and tropical fruit tasting plate.

day_by_day.notes: A private charter flight from Quepos/Manuel Antonio to Puerto Jiménez (gateway to Corcovado) takes approximately 30 minutes and is highly recommended over the long road transfer. Corcovado requires an official park guide — confirm this is arranged through the lodge. Wear sturdy closed-toe hiking shoes and bring a dry bag.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning guided wildlife walk on the eco-lodge's private reserve trails. The Osa Peninsula's biodiversity rivals Corcovado itself — spot scarlet macaws in flight, poison dart frogs on the forest floor, and spider monkeys in the canopy. Photography-focused guide available upon request.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided kayaking or snorkeling excursion in the Golfo Dulce — a rare tropical fjord known for its calm, warm waters and exceptional marine biodiversity. Spot dolphins, sea turtles, and exotic reef fish. Return to the lodge for a final afternoon of relaxation on the jungle-view infinity pool terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Premium farewell experience at the eco-lodge: a private jungle dinner set up in a forest clearing or on the lodge's elevated deck. A personal chef prepares a custom multi-course meal by candlelight surrounded by the sounds of the Osa rainforest — a truly once-in-a-lifetime dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Full lodge breakfast: freshly made smoothies, tropical fruit, eggs cooked to order, gallo pinto, and locally roasted coffee.
meals.lunch: Post-kayaking lunch at the lodge: ceviche of the day, grilled plantains with local cheese, and fresh coconut water.
meals.dinner: Private jungle dinner experience: amuse-bouche of local flavors, fresh Osa Peninsula seafood crudo, slow-roasted local pork with tropical fruit reduction, and a showstopping dessert featuring Osa cacao and local honey.

day_by_day.notes: This is the final full adventure day — take time to absorb the extraordinary environment. Request a final consultation with the lodge's resident naturalist for a personalized debrief on all wildlife encountered during the trip. Consider purchasing locally made conservation-supporting artisan crafts from the lodge gift shop.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise from the eco-lodge's viewing deck — the Osa Peninsula sunrise over the Golfo Dulce is spectacular. Enjoy a slow, leisurely final breakfast and complete any last-minute packing. Private transfer or charter flight back to San José / Juan Santamaría International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: If the departure flight allows time, enjoy a final stop in San José for a curated visit to the Jade Museum or the Gold Museum in the historic city center, or relax in the VIP lounge at the airport (Priority Pass or premium lounge access recommended). Alternatively, arrange a final premium lunch at a top San José restaurant before check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Costa Rica with extraordinary memories of 13 days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, and world-class luxury. A private airport transfer ensures a seamless final journey to the departure terminal.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the eco-lodge: a full spread of tropical favorites — açaí bowls, fresh pastries, eggs Benedict, and a final cup of Costa Rica's finest coffee.
meals.lunch: If time permits in San José: lunch at Sikwa Restaurant (indigenous-inspired Costa Rican fine dining) or Nuema restaurant for a memorable farewell meal.
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure from Juan Santamaría Airport. Confirm charter or transfer timing the night before to account for any weather delays from the Osa Peninsula. Consider purchasing premium Costa Rican coffee, local chocolate, and artisan crafts as departure gifts. Ensure all wildlife-related souvenirs comply with CITES regulations — no animal products.
